statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-53669 (GHSA-wrjc-x8rr-h8h6): react-router's earlier fix for CVE-2025-68470 missed paths that start with a backslash, so attacker-supplied paths passed to <Link> or useNavigate could still navigate to an external site. It is fixed in react-router 7.18.0 by pull request 15176, which changes the absolute-URL check from /^(?:[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:|\/\/)/i to /^(?:[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:|[\\/]{2})/i and adds a protocol-relative check /^[\\/]{2}/: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/security/advisories/GHSA-wrjc-x8rr-h8h6, https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/pull/15176, https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/releases/tag/react-router@7.18.0 . We read every published jaeger-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository: 21 builds, 2.19.0-r1 to the current 2.23.0-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64, every download checked against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/jaeger, a Go program. That program embeds the prebuilt assets of the jaeger-ui release with the same version number as gzip-compressed files; we decompressed every gzip stream in /usr/bin/jaeger and searched the JavaScript. Every build of one Jaeger version carries an identical bundle, and a search of the uncompressed binary finds none of the strings below, so there is no uncompressed copy. The bundle sets __reactRouterVersion to 7.16.0 in 2.19.0-r1 to 2.19.0-r4, 7.18.0 in 2.20.0-r0 to 2.20.0-r5 and 7.18.2 from 2.21.0-r0, matching the react-router versions locked by jaeger-ui v2.19.0 and v2.20.0 and later: https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.19.0/package-lock.json, https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.20.0/pnpm-lock.yaml . In 2.19.0-r1 to 2.19.0-r4 the bundle contains the old absolute-URL expression (used by both its isAbsoluteUrl helper and <Link>) and not the new ones; from 2.20.0-r0 it contains the new absolute-URL and protocol-relative expressions and not the old one. 2.20.0-r0 is the first fixed build for this owner.
